P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged but nothing from it was played back - 'I already, of course, saw your application, but I would just love to hear everything from you.' The frame ran to two of four parts: 'where you're at, where you want to go. If it's a good fit, I'll get you through it. If not, also perfectly fine.' Frame agreement and the open question both clean.

P2.evidence: Solid on most of the phase. Occupation and the desk-bound nature of it were both established, current training was pinned down precisely (three to four times a week, 5:30am, 12 kg, two months), results were probed, and nutrition was worked through meal by meal including a protein estimate. The injury question was the best-executed check on the call - 'Do you feel like anything with mobility is coming up for you?' followed by a 1-10 severity scale and duration - which is exactly how it surfaced the year of untreated back pain. Against that: height was never asked, age only in passing, general health conditions and hereditary risk were never raised, the lactose intolerance was volunteered, and sleep and energy were not asked of a man with three small children who wakes at 5:30 to train.

P3.evidence: The bridge question ran properly and did real work: 'Lots of people are 46 or like 50, like, you know what? It's whatever. It comes with age and they blame it on that... So why do you feel like, you know what? I'm not okay with it?' That produced the confidence material - a lifelong self-image as a skinny, weak-looking man - and the rep followed it to the children, who watch him train and are 'a little bit proud of their father'. The future-state question ran too. The gap is the reflect-back: the rep summarised commitment rather than naming the real driver back to him, so 'this isn't about muscle, it's about not being the weak thin kid' was never said.

P4.evidence: Contains the sharpest single question of the batch. When the prospect explained five inactive years by saying he had no time, the rep asked 'is it really time or is more so priority?' and got the honest answer: 'we prioritize, let's say, family ahead of ourselves... there's no time for myself.' The prospect then named his own structural gap unprompted - 'after a limit or a level, it's hard to have a progress alone, because there's no checkup, no feedback' - which is precisely the gap the offer fills. Only P4f did not run.

P5.evidence: The two checks were merged into one softened question - 'would you be okay with it not changing... for the next six months to a year?' - and the answer that came back was effectively no consequence at all: 'I would already feel healthy, strong,' followed by 'If anything happens after today, I would, of course, continue and buy new stuff and watch more videos and try to do the best I can.' That is a prospect saying out loud that he will be fine either way and will carry on alone. The rep did not work it; he converted it into agreement - 'You're here to commit, you're here to stay and you're going to do it anyway. That's good.' No why-not, no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran and was tied to his specific outcomes: 'do you feel like when we get that all in place, it's going to help you get rid of the stiffness, also potentially lower the back pain, but also just build up more muscle and get your confidence up?' The answer was hedged - 'Yeah, definitely, yeah, hopefully' - and the go-all-in question was never asked. The script says hesitation returns you to Phase 5, and there were two open hesitations here: the hedged yes, and the earlier statement that he would continue on his own regardless. Neither was revisited before the price.

P11.evidence: The best P11 in the batch, and still incomplete. A $100 down payment was taken live and confirmed by both parties, but $5,900 of the $6,000 was left to a link the next morning contingent on funds moving from savings. The Trevor onboarding call was actually booked, for 7:15pm the following evening, and the invite was confirmed received - the only time this check is hit anywhere in this batch. The agreement could not be signed on the call and the rep explained the sequencing honestly: 'that's the reason I can't do that now, but when you've paid that, then you will get an agreement.' The community invite was deferred behind the signature; only the onboarding questionnaire went out live.

objection_plays.detail: A liquidity objection rather than a capacity one - the money exists, it is in savings and it was the end of the month. The rep asked cash on hand ('What do you have in the checking at the moment?'), tested a mid-point ('do you think you have 1200 on your account, USD?') and then stepped down to $100. That is the cash-on-hand question and nothing else from the financial picture, which was probably right here, but the isolate never ran and no permission question was asked before probing the prospect's bank balances.

Script gap on clinical fit, in its most serious form in this corpus. The prospect disclosed a year of 6-7/10 sacroiliac and low lumbar joint pain and stated plainly that he has not been assessed: 'I have to go to the doctor probably.' There is no step in the process that stops a sale on that disclosure or requires clearance, so instead the rep argued against the prospect's own correct instinct that he needs medical treatment, using Trevor's injury story and a claim about another client's hernia pain, and then promised the pain would reduce.

Second script gap, the free-substitute problem. The prospect has been getting real results for two months from free short-form videos and self-bought kettlebells, follows a second free creator he named as Rokas, and said explicitly that he would continue alone if nothing came of the call. There is no play for a prospect whose free alternative is demonstrably working, and none was improvised.

notes: Discovery was strong - the priority-versus-time question in Phase 4 is the best coaching moment in the batch and the injury severity scale is exactly how that check should be run. Two failures. Phase 5 produced an explicit no-consequence answer plus a statement that he would carry on alone, and the rep read it as commitment instead of returning to it. And the handling of the back pain inverted the rep's job: the prospect arrived with a correct and cautious read of his own condition and left having been persuaded out of it. The close mechanics were the cleanest of the week, including the only Trevor booking made all batch.
